chunks: And it was narrated from Abī Wallād al-Ḥannāṭ that he said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought two men, each of whom had accused the other regarding his body, so he waived the hadd punishment from both of them and administered taʿzīr to them."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam relating the ruling
key_terms.أَبِي وَلَّادٍ الْحَنَّاطِ: Abī Wallād al-Ḥannāṭ, the transmitter named in the report
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, the judge in this case
key_terms.عَزَّرَهُمَا: he administered discretionary disciplinary punishment to them both

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two people mutually accuse each other of bodily slander?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding two men who mutually accused one another with bodily slander. Because the accusation was mutual, the fixed hadd punishment was not carried out upon them; instead, both were given discretionary disciplinary punishment.
